dialogue.title: Opening a Bank Account
dialogue.context: Ahmed visits Chase Bank to open his first U.S. bank account. Sarah, a bank representative, helps him.

lines.speaker: Sarah
lines.text: Good afternoon! Welcome to Chase Bank. How can I help you today?

lines.speaker: Ahmed
lines.text: Hello. I'd like to open a bank account. This is my first account in the United States.

lines.speaker: Sarah
lines.text: Great! I can help you with that. We have two main types: checking and savings. Do you know which one you need?

lines.speaker: Ahmed
lines.text: I'm not sure. What's the difference?

lines.speaker: Sarah
lines.text: A checking account is for everyday use - paying bills, buying things. A savings account is for keeping money you don't need right now.

lines.speaker: Ahmed
lines.text: I need to pay my rent and bills, so checking account, right?

lines.speaker: Sarah
lines.text: Exactly! You can also get a debit card with your checking account to buy things at stores.

lines.speaker: Ahmed
lines.text: Perfect. What documents do I need to open it?

lines.speaker: Sarah
lines.text: I need two forms of ID - your passport or driver's license, and your social security card or work permit. Do you have those?

lines.speaker: Ahmed
lines.text: Yes, I have my passport and social security card. Is there a monthly fee?

lines.speaker: Sarah
lines.text: There's a $12 monthly fee, but we waive it if you have direct deposit from your job. Do you get paid by direct deposit?

lines.speaker: Ahmed
lines.text: Yes, my paycheck goes directly to my bank. So no fee for me, right?

lines.speaker: Sarah
lines.text: That's correct! No fee as long as you have direct deposit. Let's get started with your application.

listening_exercises.transcript: Our checking account includes free online banking and a debit card. There's a $12 monthly maintenance fee, but we waive it if you maintain a minimum balance of $1,500 or have direct deposit. You get unlimited check writing and access to over 16,000 ATMs nationwide.
listening_exercises.question: How can you avoid the monthly fee?
options: Keep $1,500 in the account or have direct deposit
Use the ATM 10 times per month

listening_exercises.transcript: To use the ATM, first insert your card with the chip facing up. Enter your 4-digit PIN. Select the transaction you want - withdraw cash, check balance, or deposit. For cash withdrawals, select the amount you need. Remember to take your card and your cash when you're done.
listening_exercises.question: What should you do first when using an ATM?

listening_exercises.transcript: A savings account earns interest on your money - the bank pays you a small amount for keeping money with them. The interest rate is currently 0.5% per year. There's no monthly fee if you keep at least $300 in your account. You can make up to six withdrawals per month.
listening_exercises.question: What does a savings account do?

speaking_tasks.prompt: Imagine you're at a bank. Record yourself saying: 'I'd like to open a checking account. What documents do I need? Is there a monthly fee?' Practice speaking clearly.
speaking_tasks.example: Hello, I'd like to open a checking account. This is my first account in the United States. What documents do I need to bring? Also, is there a monthly fee for the account? Thank you for your help.

speaking_tasks.prompt: Explain the difference between a checking account and a savings account. Record yourself speaking for at least 30 seconds.
speaking_tasks.example: A checking account is for everyday money. You use it to pay bills and buy things. You can get a debit card. A savings account is different. It's for saving money you don't need right now. It earns interest, which means the bank pays you a little bit of money. Most people have both types of accounts.

writing_tasks.prompt: Write 5 sentences about why having a bank account is important. Use phrases like: 'A bank account helps me...', 'I can...', 'It's safer than...'
writing_tasks.example: A bank account is very important. A bank account helps me pay my bills on time. I can use a debit card instead of carrying cash. It's safer than keeping money at home. I can save money for emergencies. Many jobs require direct deposit to a bank account.

writing_tasks.prompt: You want to open a bank account. Write 4 questions you would ask the bank employee. Start each question with: 'What...?', 'How...?', 'Is there...?', or 'Can I...?'
writing_tasks.example: What documents do I need to open an account? How do I deposit money into my account? Is there a monthly fee? Can I get a debit card with this account?

grammar_focus.title: 'I'd like to' for Polite Requests
grammar_focus.explanation: 'I'd like to' = 'I would like to' - very polite way to ask for something. Better than 'I want'.
examples: I'd like to open an account. (polite, correct)
I want to open an account. (okay, less polite)
I'd like to check my balance. (polite)
I'd like to speak with a manager. (polite)

practice.sentence: ___ to apply for a credit card.

grammar_focus.title: Questions with 'Can I' and 'Do I'
grammar_focus.explanation: Use 'Can I...?' to ask if something is possible. Use 'Do I...?' to ask about requirements.
examples: Can I use any ATM? (is it possible?)
Do I need two forms of ID? (is it required?)
Can I open an account online? (is it possible?)
Do I have to pay a fee? (is it required?)

practice.sentence: ___ I use this card at any store?
___ I need a social security number?

grammar_focus.title: Present Simple for Banking Actions
grammar_focus.explanation: Use present simple to describe regular banking activities and account features.
examples: The bank opens at 9 AM. (regular schedule)
I deposit my paycheck every Friday. (regular action)
This account earns 0.5% interest. (account feature)
ATMs charge a fee. (general fact)

cultural_notes: Most Americans have at least one bank account. It's difficult to function without one.
Banks are insured by the FDIC up to $250,000, so your money is safe even if the bank fails.
Never share your PIN or banking passwords with anyone, including family.
Many banks have apps that let you deposit checks by taking a photo with your phone.
Credit unions are similar to banks but are non-profit and often have lower fees.
It's normal to have both a checking account (for spending) and a savings account (for saving).
